No collision: `natal` has no sugar-cane cell in any year, so nothing is double counted.

STRUCTURAL, FROM AN INDEPENDENT SOURCE. fao1952 `Union of South Africa` horses read 778 thousand at 1937 -- equal to Mitchell's own `south africa` 1937 horses (778,000), which identifies the column -- and 679 thousand at 1950, equal to this label's 1949 figure (679,000) and within 0.5% of its 1950 one (676,000). Mitchell's `south africa` has no horse value in 1938-1958, exactly the years `natal` fills, and the `natal` values run continuously from the national 778,000 (1937) to 472,000 (1959). Natal's own pre-Union count was 40,000-67,000 over 1900-1908. The 1957 `natal` pig value (16,000) sits BESIDE a real `south africa` pig value, so it is not this shape and is not relabelled; it stays unrouted.

PRESENT BOUNDARIES FOR RYE, PRE-WAR FOR FLAX: fao1952's USSR is mixed by item (source_conventions.csv, fao1952/*/*). Its 1934-38 rye averages are 25,870 thousand ha and 25,500 thousand t, against iia `russian federation`'s own 1934-38 USSR (the boundary of the time) 22,790 thousand ha and 20,499 thousand t: 1.14x and 1.24x. Adding what the 1939-45 annexations grew on their pre-war owners' own 1934-38 series (juan: Estonia+Latvia+Lithuania 928, the Finnish cession 28, Bessarabia/N. Bukovina net of S. Dobruja 172, Ruthenia 20, the Polish and German territories 1,923 thousand ha) gives 25,860 thousand ha, which fao1952's figure matches to 1.000 (tonnes 1.07). The same test puts flax fibre on the OLD boundary (0.99x iia, 0.90x with the gains), so no alias can serve the label: rye alone is relabelled to `USSR present boundaries`, which routes back_cast to F228-1945-1991; every other USSR pre-war item stays on F228-1921-1940. Period rows (year null, 1934-1938) are taken because the whole period lies inside the rule. Measured with fao52audit/ussr.py on consolidated_layer_b.parquet, 2026-09-24.

PRESENT BOUNDARIES. fao1952's 1937 USSR `population total` is 188,656 thousand. The Soviet census of January 1939 counted about 170.6 million on the pre-annexation boundary, and 1937 is two years earlier; the Baltic states, eastern Poland, Bessarabia/N. Bukovina and the Finnish cession added some 20 million. The figure is therefore the post-war territory, as the rye series is (see the `rye` rule), and the four 1937 population indicators (total, agricultural, agricultural occupied, female agricultural) share one column. Relabelled to `USSR present boundaries` -> back_cast F228-1945-1991; the pre-war horse, flax and linseed rows keep the `USSR` label and F228-1921-1940.
